overview.headline: Comparing sunlight and chemical energy pathways that fuel life

keyPoints.point: Sunlit food webs show plants use sunlight to make food through photosynthesis
keyPoints.quote: The majority of life on Earth is based on a food web which revolves around the Sun, as plants use sunlight to make food via photosynthesis.

keyPoints.point: Microbes rely on chemical energy through chemosynthesis where sunlight is absent
keyPoints.quote: organisms instead rely on primary production through a process called chemosynthesis, which runs on chemical energy.

keyPoints.point: Matter cannot be created or destroyed so reactant atoms must form products
keyPoints.quote: the law of conservation of matter states that matter cannot be created or destroyed.

keyTerms.gloss: process where plants convert carbon dioxide and water into food using sunlight
keyTerms.quote: Photosynthesis: The process used by plants to convert carbon dioxide and water into oxygen and sugars (food), using energy from the sun.

keyTerms.gloss: process where microbes create food using energy from chemical reactions
keyTerms.quote: Chemosynthesis: The process by which microbes create sugars (food) using energy released from chemical reactions.

keyTerms.gloss: organism able to make food from raw materials and energy as producer
keyTerms.quote: Autotroph: Organisms that are able to make their own food from raw materials and energy, also known as producers.

keyTerms.gloss: starting materials that change in a chemical reaction
keyTerms.quote: Reactants: A substance that changes in a chemical reaction.
